article_lead.description: a model that links group-specific parameters through an uncertain population distribution so sparse groups can share information

new_bank_questions.title: A class mean with partial pooling
new_bank_questions.body: For a normal hierarchy with known population mean μ=40, between-class variance τ²=9 and within-class variance σ²=36, a class of four has sample mean 55. Find its conditional posterior weight on its own mean, posterior mean and posterior variance.
new_bank_questions.answer: The weight is nτ²/(σ²+nτ²)=4(9)/(36+4(9))=1/2. The posterior mean is (1/2)55+(1/2)40=47.5. The variance is σ²τ²/(σ²+nτ²)=36(9)/72=4.5. This is conditional on the supplied population parameters.

new_bank_questions.title: Conditional independence can hide marginal dependence
new_bank_questions.body: Let θ be uniform on [0,1], and conditionally on θ let Y₁ and Y₂ be independent Bernoulli(θ). Find P(Y₁=1), P(Y₁=1,Y₂=1), and Cov(Y₁,Y₂). Are the two observations marginally independent?
new_bank_questions.answer: Eθ=1/2, so P(Y₁=1)=1/2. Conditional independence gives P(Y₁=1,Y₂=1)=Eθ²=1/3. Thus Cov(Y₁,Y₂)=1/3-(1/2)²=1/12>0. Sharing an uncertain θ makes them marginally dependent.
